subject.title: fix(agents): preserve runtime tool inheritance tokens for spawned subagents (#85030)

question: Should the final-concrete-tool implementation in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92521 own this fix, or should this branch be reworked to the same boundary?
rationale: The selector-preservation design runs before later security-relevant filters, while the related PR centralizes inheritance after those filters; maintainers should select one canonical authorization model.

options.title: Use final concrete tools
options.body: Prefer the proof-positive related PR's post-materialization refresh, confirm it covers all spawn entry paths, and close or narrow this competing branch.

options.title: Rework this branch
options.body: Replace selector preservation with a shared final-surface refresh and supply exact-head positive and deny-path runtime proof.

recommendation.title: Use final concrete tools
recommendation.body: Prefer the proof-positive related PR's post-materialization refresh, confirm it covers all spawn entry paths, and close or narrow this competing branch.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent work spans all three affected resolution surfaces and the current-main contracts involved in this choice.
